conclusion: Gate-5 property 6 as written has no truth value: the box is a free parameter of the sentence, and holding the sigma-band fixed at [0.7, 0.9] while changing only the height window flips the verdict between DISTINGUISHES (t in [85.5, 85.9], where Davenport-Heilbronn has a zero and zeta does not) and VACUOUS (t in [10, 14] and [40, 44], where neither does). Every repair that gives it a truth value and still distinguishes collapses to either RH itself or the Euler product, so property 6 does not look like an independent sixth property but a local shadow of properties 4 and 5.
confidence: High for the well-posedness finding and for the boxes actually run: it rests only on winding numbers of xi and of f, both cheap, both integral to well under the routine's 1e-6 residual guard, and the flip needs only Davenport-Heilbronn, which is the arm that finished. Lower, and explicitly labelled partial, for what the Epstein rivals do in the two high boxes B1 and B3: those were not run. Neither can overturn the conclusion (B3's VACUOUS is already forced by Davenport-Heilbronn alone, since gate #3 asks the structure be ungrantable to every rival; an Epstein absence in B1 would only strengthen the box-dependence claim). The reading that the previous attempt died of the same precision defect rather than of contour length is a diagnosis consistent with the symptom, not a verified account of a run I did not observe.

threads.what: Locate the lowest zero of a discriminant -23 Epstein zeta in sigma > 1.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Davenport and Heilbronn proved such zeros exist for class number greater than one, but this tree cites that rather than computes it. A located zero turns the only checkable repair of property 6 from a citation into a measurement, and gives the battery a sigma > 1 box with real discriminating power.

threads.what: The battery counts Davenport-Heilbronn on f and the other three on their completions.
threads.why_it_might_matter: Harmless in sigma > 0, where the completion factors are zero-free and pole-free, so it affected nothing here. It is not harmless for any future box reaching sigma <= 0, where the trivial zeros enter and the two conventions genuinely differ.

core_candidates.what: A height-aware accuracy guard on zeta.epstein.epstein_completed. It returns Lambda_Q by a Mellin split whose last two terms are O(1/t) against an answer decaying like exp(-pi t / 2), so roughly 0.6822 * t digits cancel and the caller is told nothing. At the documented dps = 20 the value has four correct digits at t = 44 and the phase is noise above t ~ 30.
core_candidates.why_reusable: Every argument-principle count over an Epstein zeta goes through this function, and a silently wrong phase does not produce a wrong answer, it produces a call that never returns. This defect very likely cost the previous attempt at this same question its fifty minutes, and it cost this one about an hour.
core_candidates.first_step: Either raise the internal guard to dps + ceil(0.6822 * |Im s|), or return the estimated lost digits alongside the value so a caller can refuse. A test pinning the dps-20-vs-dps-80 disagreement at t = 44 makes the defect visible either way.

core_candidates.what: An evaluation or depth ceiling on zeta.epstein.count_zeros_box that converts non-convergence into the ArithmeticError the routine already documents.
core_candidates.why_reusable: The adaptive bisection recurses to max_depth 45 per segment when the phase is noise, so a mis-precisioned input hangs rather than fails. Every caller of the argument principle in this tree inherits that. A counter that raises once total evaluations pass a multiple of the forced segment count turns a fifty-minute hang into a two-second diagnosis, and it is a dozen lines.
core_candidates.first_step: Thread a budget through _edge_variation and _arg_variation; raise ArithmeticError naming the segment when it is exhausted, which is the same failure class the docstring already promises for an undersampled edge.

core_candidates.what: A cheap preflight that reports per-evaluation cost of each battery function at the heights a proposed box will reach, before the box is committed.
core_candidates.why_reusable: The whole difference between this run and the prior attempt is that the cost model was measured first: total boundary length times per-evaluation cost at the box's maximum height, not box area. That took ninety seconds to measure and it is the same measurement any future battery hunt needs.
core_candidates.first_step: Time each interface's completed() at three heights and print the implied cost of a candidate box from the module's own forced-step formula. It is about thirty lines and it belongs next to battery(), not inside a hunt.

notes_for_operator: Two things worth knowing beyond the science. First, the preregistration rule did real work here and also bent: dps = 20 was fixed in MISSION.md and turned out to be unusable for the Epstein arm, so the run deviated to a height-dependent rule and recorded the deviation in probe.py and RESULTS.md rather than editing the preregistration. The justification is independent of any answer (it comes from an accuracy table, not from a count), but an operator comparing the three parallel agents should know that this branch's dps is not the dps it preregistered. Second, the two core candidates above are both defects in zeta/epstein.py, which this hunt's scope forbids it to touch; they are reported and not fixed. Independence was kept: no other hunt/gate5-p6-* branch or hunts/gate5_p6_* directory was read.
